#4069. Deborah Ann Woll Will Reprise Her Role As Laufey In Amazon's God Of War Series

Deborah Ann Woll, likely best known as Karen Page in Daredevil and Daredevil: Born Again, has just been cast as Laufey in the upcoming live-action God of War series. It's a perfect fit, not just because she's a great actress – Woll already portrays the character in the video games.

The live-action God of War series is currently in production, and after a series of headlines about Kratos, it's refreshing to get some news about his late wife, Faye. Also known as Laufey, she dies right before 2018's God of War (which the show is based on) begins. The game centers on a journey between Kratos and his son to spread Faye's ashes from the highest peak in the realms.

Faye is not present in 2018's God of War, but she appears in God of War Ragnarök in flashback and dream sequences. In this game, she's played by Deborah Ann Woll, an oddly high-profile casting for a relatively minor character. It all made sense earlier this year, however, when we learned Woll will reprise her role as the star of God of War Laufey, which tells Faye's story as she fights through a mythological underworld.

It's a cool piece of news, and it implies that Faye will have more of a presence in the series than in the first game, where she never appears at all. As for what shape that presence takes, we have no idea.

Woll joins the likes of Alastair Duncan, who plays Mimir and will also reprise his role. The two don't really interact in the games, however, so it's unlikely to see them share the screen in the series.

The main news around Prime Video's God of War is about its protagonist. Originally announced as Ryan Hurst, the actor suffered a serious injury on the set of the show and was replaced by Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy, Glass Onion) in August. Other key cast members include Callum Vinson as Atreus, Sonya Walger as Freya, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, and Ed Skrein as Baldur.

For more God of War, you can look forward to Woll's portrayal of Faye in God of War Laufey, though it recently got delayed.

#4067. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4066. One Of Our Favorite Action Games From Gamescom, Showa American Story, Has Been Delayed To 2027

Showa American Story is set in a world where Japan's 1980s economic prowess was strong enough to purchase America, and so it did. Taking place in Neo Yokohama, formerly Hollywood, this raunchy, zany action game was one of our favorites at Gamescom 2026, but unfortunately, we'll have to wait a little longer than expected to experience more of this adventure.

That's because developer Nekcom Entertainment and publisher 4Divinity have revealed that Showa American Story has been delayed to next year. Originally due out sometime this year (though it became clear that wasn't going to happen given the radio silence as we near the year's end), Showa American Story will now launch on PlayStation 5 and PC on October 28, 2027.

"Reaching this milestone after five years of development means a lot to our entire team," the studio writes in a statement. "With core game content now complete, we're dedicating our full focus to polishing and optimizing the experience so that when you step into Showa American Story, it feels cohesive, responsive, and complete. Thank you for your continued support, enthusiasm, and patience along the way. We can't wait to welcome you on October 28, 2027."

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Showa American Story hands-on preview from this year's Gamescom. After that, check out our list of the top 10 action games to play right now.

#4065. Rockstar’s Rob Nelson Explains Why You Can’t Wield GTA 6's Chainsaws

GTA 6 is being celebrated for more reasons every day, and rightfully so. However, the most striking thing about the game, since it’s the first thing you see and it’s hitting you over the head every second you’re looking at it, is how stunning it is. That realism is one of the reasons why the option to make Jason and Lucia hyper-violent is taken out of the player’s hands.

Rockstar producer Rob Nelson revealed the level of thinking that went into not only some of the endless things you can do in Leonida, but also some of the things you can’t in an interview with VGC. One of the things Nelson discussed was the decision to not include weapons that would allow for a heightened level of violence that have been present in previous GTA entries, like chainsaws and katanas.

Despite a mountain of leaks, Rockstar managed to keep one of GTA 6’s biggest plot points a secret throughout all of its development.

“As far as the chainsaw – I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson explains, adding, “It’s not a resource thing.” Other omissions, such as not being able to play games like darts or bowling, were confirmed to have been left on the cutting room floor because Rockstar simply didn’t think it was worth the time and effort when those resources could be put to better use elsewhere.

The realism that you get with GTA 6 means even standard stuff that has to be in the games, like shooting someone or hitting them with a blunt object, is far more visceral than it has ever been before. When coupled with how much more grounded GTA 6’s lead characters are, giving them the option to carve someone up with a chainsaw just doesn’t fit.

“Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that – what’s that going to look like?” Nelson continues, adding, “You’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance, it really just depends, you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible,” when asked about chainsaws existing in Leonida, but Rockstar choosing not to let players interact with them at all.

It’s a tricky line to walk. A huge part of GTA has always been about players doing whatever they like, and going “psycho,” as Nelson puts it. Once I was done with GTA San Andreas's story, I input cheats to give pedestrians weapons and then made them riot. The whole point of that game for me after that was for it to be as chaotic and unrealistic as possible.

That was a long time ago. Sure, GTA has always been violent, but its violence has never been realised with the same realism as it is in GTA 6. Not just the way it looks, but the way you play and the repercussions that come along with everything you do. Jason and Lucia are the closest the series has ever seen to protagonists that act like real people. They’re not caricatures like the leads in previous GTA games. They might be criminals, but as Nelson says, they’re not psychos who are going to fight their way out of a situation with a chainsaw. It wouldn’t make sense for them, and it no longer makes sense for GTA.

The cards you're collecting in GTA 6 will soon be available to buy for real.

#4063. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4062. Guide: 43 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' eShop Sale (US)

Every game we scored 9/10 or higher, plus a personal pick

Just a reminder that this sale runs until December 2nd, so you've still got plenty of time if you're after a bargain but can't bear the thought of the Black Friday crowds. Carry on!

With Nintendo launching its Black Friday sale on the European eShop earlier this week, we knew it was only a matter of time before our friends in North America got some savings of their own. And what do you know, they have!

Nintendo's 'Adventure Awaits' sale is now live on the North American storefront, with discounts across a bunch of first- and third-party delights. It'll be sticking around until 2nd December at 11:59pm PT, so you still have a couple of weeks to make the most of it.

Just like with the EU sale, we have assembled the following list of every game in the Adventure Awaits offer that we awarded a 9/10 or higher. We've also added a personal pick from the 8/10s at the end, because we couldn't see it go unmentioned.

As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim is a wonderful achievement for dynamic storytelling, as it puts forth a compelling and multifaceted narrative that’ll keep you guessing right up until the very end.

This excellent story, combined with enjoyable combat portions, a striking art style, and some top-notch voice acting make for an experience that you shouldn't miss. It’s the kind of game that’ll have you wishing that you could play it again for the first time, just so all its best elements could be new again.

Aegis Defenders is a fantastic game, brilliantly blending the tower defence and platforming genres in a unique way to produce a memorable and enjoyable experience.

Lovable characters, interesting lore, plenty of secrets, engaging gameplay, and gorgeous presentation combine to make this a must-have for your Switch, a real gem on the eShop.

AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.

Even with some minor control issues, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.

The Nintendo eShop would be a considerably more exciting and interesting place if it were packed full of games like Ape Out. It’s a refreshingly original experience that more than deserves a place in any Switch owner’s library.

Difficult, frenetic gameplay, strong art direction, and an even stronger jazz drum soundtrack make this the sort of memorable game that you’ll likely keep coming back to over and over for another few runs in arcade mode. Ape Out gets a strong recommendation to anyone looking for a distinct and unforgettable game for their Switch collection; it’s a bit of an acquired taste, but well worth your time.

BALL x PIT is a tremendous brew of so many ideas it ought to collapse under the confusion. However, it operates in such perfect balance that it appeals both to the one-more-go instinct and to more cerebral planning and creativity. Kenny Sun Studios set itself a heck of a challenge but, fortunately, hasn’t dropped the ball.

It's out on Switch 2, too - and the upgrade is free.

Card Shark is the kind of game that at first blush seems like it just won’t work. Lots of dialogue bookended by brief, simplistic minigame sequences seems like it would make for an experience that would lose its lustre quickly, yet we couldn’t put it down.

Witty writing, high-stakes gameplay, and a gorgeous art style all come together here to make for a game that’s well-executed and unique in its appeal. If you’re looking to try something awesome that notably bucks most modern gaming trends, Card Shark is absolutely something we’d recommend, well worth your time and money.

Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent new character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface issues which are easily ignored.

At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

It's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

There isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

Dark Souls: Remastered is a faithful remaster of a touchstone in video game design that improves overall performance of the original release while preserving all of the character traits that made it such a memorable experience. While it’s no less forgiving — and its menus are a little fiddly — this slick Nintendo Switch iteration offers an excellent way to experience Lordran’s ultra-challenging odyssey in true handheld form.

Plus, there's a Solaire of Astora amiibo. Praise the Sun, indeed.

This is an excellent port of a game that feels like it’s found a natural home on Switch thanks to a plethora of control options and the console’s natural facility with vertical orientation. Short of popping your 4K TV on its side, Switch offers the very best way to play Downwell.

Its roguelike structure and twitch platforming might not be for everyone, but you should really give it a chance. For our money, Downwell is a modern classic that should be in everyone’s collection; for the pocket change asking price, it's a steal.

Along with the expected multiplayer modes (ranked and casual battles), Faeria delivers a compulsive, interesting and frankly enormously fun card battle experience. While not the easiest game to explain, it's an impressive teaching tool for itself, but never feels overwrought or tiresome in said education. Of the card games we've enjoyed on Switch, Faeria is easily the highlight of the bunch and deserves to do well. It's a full-featured package and stands out as an excellent card/board/strategy experience. If you want to play a fantasy card game on Switch, we'd recommend this one first.

Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

Heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This new release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

Granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

Invisible, Inc. is a brilliant little tactics game, right up there with Into the Breach and XCOM – if not even better. The bite-sized structure belies a deceptively complex and meaningful game, where all your decisions ultimately mean something significant for that final desperate attack.

If you enjoy stealth or tactics games – or you're simply looking for a way into either genre – then Invisible, Inc. deserves your attention.

In a cynical era where nostalgia is pumped for all its worth with endless soulless remasters, Katamari Damacy Reroll serves up an engaging and rewarding game that hasn’t let any of its original charm or personality be lost in the transition from one platform to another.

With support for gyro controls and multiplayer — not to mention a degree of performance that sees it run smoothly in both handheld and docked mode — this Switch edition is easily the best way to play it outside of blowing the dust off your old PS2.

Altogether now: Naa na-na na-naa na na na...

An absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

Easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a great big colourful joyride of an adventure for our little pink pal.

This first fully three-dimensional mainline entry in the franchise is bursting at the seams with fun and inventiveness, managing to transpose everything we know and love about past Kirby games to this all-new arena whilst adding plenty of delightful new aspects as it goes.

Mouthful Mode is daftly entertaining, each and every level is packed full of secrets and dripping in wonderful detail, and there are enough side activities, collectibles, and co-op fun here to keep you entertained and coming back for more for a good long while.

Whether you're playing on Switch 1 or via the excellent Star-Crossed World expansion on Switch 2 (with upgraded visuals and 60fps performance to boot), this comes highly recommended if you're looking for a fun platformer to play with kids.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (say that five times, etc.) gives you the base game at a delicious 60fps with a whole big bunch of new content thrown in for good measure.

If you've had your fill of Forgotten Land on Switch 1, there's nothing here to warrant replaying the entire game again, but the 12 remixed areas that make up the DLC are uniformly delightful, the new transformations are excellent, and there's even new challenges for hardcore Kirby fans to get stuck into.

One of the best games on Switch and one of our favourite 3D platformers in years, polished to a sparkly sheen and packing some meaningful new content? That's a very easy recommendation and a truly excellent addition to the Switch 2's early lineup.

Buy Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World

Mark of the Ninja: Remastered is an utterly stellar stealth game and it’s lost none of the magic that made the original such a critical darling. Strong art direction, an engaging story, well-paced open gameplay, and a slew of extra content all combine to make for a near-flawless experience that you certainly won’t want to miss out on.

We’d give this game a high recommendation to all Switch owners; it’s the best stealth game money can buy in the Switch library, and one of the best ones in any console library.

Metroid Dread was a triumphant return for both Samus Aran and developer MercurySteam. This is a hugely entertaining and exquisitely designed entry that was slicker than anything we've seen from the series so far.

With a bunch of fantastic new abilities, super tense and enjoyable stealth sections, plenty of great big boss fights, and a story that long-time fans will definitely enjoy, we can't really see how this one could have been improved. Pixel nostalgia and genre impact aside, there's a very strong argument that 2D Metroid has never been better.

Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom is a tremendous accomplishment. It’s a gorgeous-looking game with a fantastic soundtrack and does its spiritual predecessors proud by nailing the Wonder Boy mechanics while still offering something that will appeal to modern audiences. As long as you can appreciate that it’s still very much an old-school game at heart and you’re going to get some 8-bit era platforming trickiness as a result, you’re going to thoroughly enjoy playing through this adventure for the 12-15 hours it’ll take you to beat it. It may not be Wonder Boy by name, but it’s definitely wonderful by nature.

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

Give us the Switch 2 Updates for Dread.....AAAAHHHH! xD

#4060. Wizards Is Only Targeting Counterfeit Cards, Not Regular MTG Proxies

There's a fine line between a proxy and a counterfeit card, and Wizards is only interested in eradicating one of them from the game of Magic.

A wave of controversy hit Magic: The Gathering this week after Wizards of the Coast revealed it is taking legal action against a group of proxy card businesses, collectively referred to as 'PrintMTG Enterprise,' that produce and sell unofficial MTG cards directly to players on several marketplaces. The lawsuit is worth $28.5 million, and it includes strict conditions if Wizards succeeds, such as handing over all card-printing equipment used in the business.

The community was immediately up in arms over the announcement, as it felt like Wizards was taking a huge step forward in a war against proxy cards, but the reality is that your average proxy card is safe, and this is actually more about counterfeit cards. Is there a difference? Yes, and it could be a costly one for 'PrintMTG Enterprises.'

The difference between a counterfeit Magic card and a proxy is that a proxy card is clearly not a real Magic card, typically because it has a plain back or doesn't use official Magic artwork on the front. In most cases, proxy cards have a plain white back, so they can't be confused with an official Magic card.

Counterfeit cards are carbon copies of the original Magic design and are intended to deceive players who aren't all that familiar with the minor details that make a Magic card legit. This can also include using the same paper stock as official Magic cards to make them feel authentic in hand, as well as any details meant to fool the eye.

It's entirely fair for Wizards of the Coast to target any seller looking to reproduce Magic cards and sell them in a condition that could be used to defraud others, and this lawsuit shouldn't be confused with Wizards taking a stance against proxy makers or users.

If you're looking for the best Secret Lair MTG Commander deck to purchase on the secondary market, we're ranking them all from worst to best.

One of the big debates that arose from this lawsuit is why now? It's fair to say that counterfeit Magic cards have been around for a long time, so why is now the time for Wizards to take a stance and look to get them off the market?

The reality is that we'll never know why, but it's a positive move for the secondary market regardless. Proxy cards, when advertised and produced correctly, aren't mistaken for regular Magic cards, and those who buy them are 100% okay with that.

Counterfeit cards become a problem when people look on typically trusted marketplaces for an official card but end up buying a counterfeit version without knowing it, because the seller is trying to make a quick buck.

This isn't to say that the companies producing these counterfeit cards do so with the intent of deceiving players in online transactions, but that's what is happening, and it needs to stop.

I've only ever purchased one counterfeit card in my time playing Magic, and it was a copy of Tibalt's Trickery. It wasn't a very expensive card, but the copy I received was clearly fake, not to the eye, but to the touch. I reported the seller, who had ghosted me after the transaction, and I got my money back, but I wonder how many players that seller managed to fool.

On the proxy front, I only own one set of proxy cards: the Goblin Storm Secret Lair Commander deck. Due to this deck selling out incredibly fast and being scalped for insane prices online, I decided to proxy it instead, but did so from a seller who clearly stated that the backs of the cards would arrive plain white, and that the paper stock used was quite thin (as a warning for when I sleeved the deck). This was perfect, because I planned to use the deck still at my local store, and with my Commander pod, I wanted to be able to say "hey, this is a proxy, does anyone have a problem with that?" as the code of honor among most groups is that, as long as you admit to what it is, there's typically no issue playing with it.

Magic is a very expensive game to get into in most formats, so proxies let you avoid extortionate secondary market prices (especially on land for Commander right now) and still play with limited-availability stuff like Goblin Storm.

Proxies are great, and they should continue to be allowed as long as certain rules are followed. I have no issue with Wizards setting a clear boundary for what a counterfeit card is and why it isn't good for the game.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4059. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or plan to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

#4058. Phil Spencer Might Not Be At Xbox Anymore, But He's Still Playing Loads Of Games

Phil Spencer is a legend of the Xbox division, having helped redefine the brand after a disastarous Xbox One launch in 2013, and spearheading such initiatives as Xbox Game Pass, Xbox backwards compatibility, crossplay, and a renewed focus on gaming rather than continuing the push towards "TV, TV, TV" that had proven so controversial.

It's very possible that without his influence, Xbox would have shut its doors over a decade ago.

News Microsoft Considered Pulling The Plug On Xbox Back In 2014

We haven't heard anything from Spencer since he announced his retirement earlier in 2026, but he's still very actively playing games on his Xbox consoles, including some of this year's new releases.

For example, he's racked up 940/1000 gamerscore in Echo Generation 2, 650/1000 in Forza Horizon 6, 585/1000 in Replaced, and he's also been playing the likes of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Gears of War: E-Day, Sopa - Tale of the Stolen Potato, Baldur's Gate 3, Vampire Crawlers and even Sunset Overdrive in recent months.

One of Phil's most beloved qualities as Xbox boss was that he proved himself to be a hardcore gamer, being someone who actively seeks to play games in his spare time. New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is somewhat the opposite, admitting back in February that she doesn't "pretend to be the best gamer" and that it's ultimately not her goal to be.

Anyway, Phil is busy enjoying his retirement right now, and we wish him all the best from everyone here at Pure Xbox. We unfortunately never got a chance to meet the man ourselves, but always admired his leadership from afar.

Here's hoping he might start hitting the interview circuit and doing what the likes of Peter Moore and Nintendo's Reggie Fils-Aimé have done in the past, as we'd love to see him sticking around the industry in some capacity going forward.

#4057. Grand Theft Auto VI Reaches Highest Concurrent Player Count Ever For PS5, More than 683 Million Hours Logged Already

Grand Theft Auto VI hasn't even been out for a week, and it's already broken so many records that it's hard to keep up. It made $3.79 billion in just 24 hours after its November 19 launch, making it the biggest entertainment launch of all time. It comes as no surprise, then, that Rockstar Games' latest crime saga is also shattering records specifically on PlayStation 5.

In a new PlayStation Blog post, the company has revealed that more than 39 million unique players have booted up GTA VI on PS5, with the game setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer games such as Helldivers II, free-to-play games like Fortnite, and single-player releases like Elden Ring. What's more, PS5 players have already logged a cumulative 683 million hours of GTA VI gameplay – that's nearly 78,000 years' worth of time.

Other records for GTA VI on PS5 include the game giving PlayStation the "largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays," and GTA VI being the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles since the game's launch.

This is likely only the beginning of records GTA VI will continue to break.

In the meantime, read Game Informer's GTA VI review to find out why it's one of the greatest games we've ever played, then read the game's first update patch notes to see what's changed. After that, read Game Informer's exclusive interview with Rockstar about the romance between Jason and Lucia, and then check out this feature on the 102 things we actually got before GTA VI. For more, head to Game Informer's GTA VI hub to make sure you don't miss any of our stories, op-eds, features, and guides for the game.

Are you playing GTA VI? Tell us the craziest thing you've experienced thus far!

#4056. GTA 6's Map Sparks Family Guy Character Comparisons With Peter Griffin

The absolutely massive map of Grand Theft Auto 6 is one that players have been theorizing about for years and have still only discovered a small portion of, despite players having already racked up 80,000 years' worth of playtime in the game on PlayStation 5 alone. While these numbers are certainly impressive, the more interesting part of Leonida is how many Easter eggs and hidden details are scattered throughout the map.

Although some of these references are more obvious, like callbacks to Miami's Dexter compared to others that could take years before being fully pieced together, one comparison to a character from one other than Family Guy made by a player online has completely changed how we see the map.

While you might need to squint to see it at first, after being compared side by side from X user gardeninqueen, GTA 6's map of Leonida state really does bear a striking resemblance to Peter Griffon from Family Guy, but more specifically his standard hands-at-the-side pose.

Although it's hard to imagine Rockstar spending over a decade working on a game just to make its entire map a Family Guy gag, the post has since gone viral with countless players backing up how similar they look and saying, "It's genuinely him" or "Oh my god I see it" when overlaying the image over top of Leonida.

The funniest part is that this isn't even the first time this has happened to Rockstar either, as players also said the same thing about Grand Theft Auto 5's map looking like Homer Simpson's head. While many players also questioned how either of these comparisons were noticed in the first place, it isn't too surprising given how rabid fans have been over map speculation since GTA 6 was revealed.

Explore our GTA 6 interactive map of Leonida: Every locations, safehouses, hidden packages and more

Although we'll likely never get an official confirmation if the unlikely similarity was intentional or not, the fact that this has happened twice now with two American animated sitcoms feels more than a little suspicious at this point.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4055. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4054. Nioh 3 Comes To Xbox In January, Second Story DLC Launches Next Month

The Nioh series celebrates its 10th anniversary next February, and developer Team Ninja is celebrating with a pair of announcements for its latest entry, Nioh 3. First, the game's second story expansion, Bloody Insurrection, launches next month. Second, the game is coming to Xbox in January, marking the franchise's debut on Microsoft's platform.

Bloody Insurrection is Nioh 3's next story expansion following Hell Rising, which launched in August, and is set to release on December 18. Set in Shimabara in 1638, players will be at the center of a conflict between rebel forces, alchemists, and yokai while encountering familiar faces from previous Nioh games. Returning characters include Tachibana Muneshige from the original Nioh, and Bloody Insurrection will serve as the conclusion of protagonist Takechiyo's story.

Bloody Insurrection also introduces new Martial Arts for each weapon type, new Transformed Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, and Summoning Seals, and a new difficulty mode called Nioh's Journey. This new difficulty option is only available if you've completed the Enlightened One's Journey third playthrough and will allow players to find Ethereal equipment drops that let them acquire the highest rarity items in the game.

Additionally, Bloody Insurrection adds new endgame content called the Battlefield of Carnage. This challenges players with climbing floors, i.e., battlefields, filled with enemies and a boss. Each floor is divided into multiple battlefields, and defeating the floor's boss grants helpful battlefield effects, which can be combined to create unique synergies as you climb higher. Defeating enemies also lets players enhance special equipment "instilled with traces of the Yokai Realm," according to Koei Tecmo, which can only be found in Battlefield of Carnage.

A new edition of the game called Nioh 3: Complete Edition arrives on January 28 and will include the base game and its two story expansions. Complete Edition will arrive on PlayStation 5, PC, and, for the first time, Xbox Series X/S. The base version of Nioh 3 is also coming to Xbox Series X/S on the same date. The original version of Nioh 3 is also on sale at a 50 percent discount on PlayStation and Steam, and the season pass is 25 percent off.

For more on Nioh 3, be sure to read our review, in which we awarded the game a 9 out of 10. You can also check out our interview with Team Ninja discussing the Hell Rising expansion.

#4053. Talking Point: Ocarina Of Time Revolutionised The 3D Swordfight, But How Does The Remake Hold Up In A Vintage Year For Clashing Blades?

Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto. Big Walk? Big deal. It’s all noise designed to distract us from 2026’s real legacy: that it’s been one of the best years on record for video game swordfighting.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword broke free of parryslop with exciting, flexible and immensely satisfying katana combat. Blood of Dawnwalker’s directional combat recreated a scintillating sense of strike-and-counterstrike rhythm rather than asking players to hide behind defensive blocks. Then Phantom Blade Zero swans in with cinematic style and a dazzling flurry of wuxia sword strikes and somersaults.

It makes it a funny time for The Hero of Time to step back into the fray. After all, the original N64 Ocarina of Time practically set the template for today’s sword-toting successors. Dark Souls, Onimusha, even Kingdom Hearts’ keyblade battles all follow in Link’s Kokiri bootprints.

Ocarina of Time famously defined the lock-on, circle strafing, and the basic choreography of action-game design. According to a 2011 Iwata Asks, that genre-defining 3D swordfighting had a charming origin story (after a fleeting moment where they considered making Ocarina of Time in first-person!). It came about thanks to a ninja show witnessed by co-director Toru Osawa and colleagues on a frankly enviable work excursion to the Toei Kyoto Studio Park.

As Osawa remembered the Japanese period film reenactment, “a number of ninja were surrounding the main samurai, and one lashed out with a kusarigama [a sickle and chain weapon]. The lead samurai caught it with his left arm, the chain stretched tight, and the ninja moved in a circle around him.”

Action choreography was the remaining issue for director Yoshiaki Koizumi. At that same ninja show, he spotted the action movie routine that helps Jackie Chan inexplicably survive every movie:

“First, one attacks while the others wait. When the first guy goes down, the next one steps in and so on [...] Watching that show at the studio park was a clue toward solving that problem. Z-targeting flags one particular opponent, telling the other enemies to wait.”

That impeccable logic meant Link was safe from being mobbed by Keese swooping from offscreen in all directions. It was such a sound design principle that it continues to underpin action games today. But I suspect modern players no longer need to be handled with Koizumi’s kid gloves. Judging by the remake, Nintendo agrees.

Consider how Nintendo changed N64 Ocarina’s Forest Temple’s ominous fight against two Wolfos. Lock on to one, its counterpart scampers obediently into the background. Not so for the remake! These newly terrifying fiends aren’t just tankier, swifter, and more aggressive: they’ll conduct somersaulting tag-team switchups at will so you’re left to deal with a full health bar – just like the Lizalfos duo.

It’s a lesson not every Ocarina successor learned. The latest Onimusha’s greatest flaw comes from how closely its mobs follow the age-old formula. Attacking one at a time, queuing up a procession of theatrical wind-up animations makes them trivially easy for a supremely talented Mushashi to attack, deflect, or even decapitate with a well-timed Issen counter. Dawnwalker’s usually not much better, sending vampire Brencis’s lackeys after you in patient succession.

In comparison, I have to commend Phantom Blade Zero for its willingness to toss out Koizumi’s Law, never passing up an opportunity to give players a well-deserved backstabbing.

But the remake’s multitude of combat changes go far beyond footwork and newly aggressive enemies. For all its modernising under-the-hood changes, playing it still feels like entering a mystical parallel universe where Sekiro never happened. I’m back with sword and shield in hand, without a high-risk, high-reward parry ability.

Even with its snappier, flashier but deeply familiar combat, it took some getting used to a gentler pace compared to more recent upstarts. I started my playthrough thoroughly parrybrained after spending nearly 100 hours playing Dawnwalker into Wolverine before finally catching up with Metroid Dread. When I returned to Hyrule, it was with fingers already twitching with anticipation at every incoming blow.

Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy.

One problem: I was ready to parry but Link wasn’t. In fact, the remake felt close to playing Dark Souls using the almost obligatory sword-and-shield build (with a parry I never learned to use properly!). As our review rightly noted, it’s laudably true to the original game, not even touching The Wind Waker’s combat-geared flourishes like the jump-spin attacks that would follow five years later.

The result is combat that feels almost like a cautious game of chess. You bait a mistake or trigger a weakness before going for the stunlock. Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy. It may no longer be dangerous to go alone, but at least we have a few tips to help up the ante – I just wouldn’t recommend a swordless run!

Along with the absent stamina and posture meters, Ocarina remake’s simpler combat blessedly ignores a more recent swordfighting innovation: light and heavy attacks. Generally, I can live without the added layer of combat timing fussiness the Soulslike dominion has given us. It also avoids the pitfalls introduced by Phantom Blade Zero, where single inputs translate into a continuous flurry of attacks that can feel unsatisfyingly disconnected from the buttons I’ve pressed.

That’s not to say I wouldn’t say no to all modern embellishments. I’d love a high-powered combo finisher such as Wind Waker’s. But don’t forget: Ocarina already had a more entertaining means to deal a slow wind-up finishing blow capable of leaving its victim in a 6ft deep crater. It’s big, it’s bad, it’s the same height as your dad: it’s the Biggoron Sword!

But no matter the size of the sword he wields, Link’s return from the past has the vibe of a strangely youthful veteran checking in on his proteges. Musashi, Coen, and Soul are the new kids on the block, but they learned everything they know from their green-tunicked, rosy-cheeked master.

And if it ever comes down to a showdown, those newcomers simply aren’t getting past Link’s guard when he hasn’t got a stamina meter to wear down.

#4052. Capcom Is Delisting Exoprimal In A Few Months, Then Killing It In 2027

Can't believe the dinosaurs are going extinct, again!

Capcom has today announced that its dinosaur PvPvE shooter Exoprimal will end service on September 29, 2027, meaning it will no longer be playable after that date. The game is also set to be delisted from digital storefronts, including the Xbox Store, on March 30, 2027.

"We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027."

Exoprimal launched on Xbox Series X|S on July 14, 2023, and suffered a pretty pants opening with only 4,995 players logging in through Steam to play Capcom's new team-based shooter.

Here's a detailed breakdown of what is going to happen to Exoprimal in the months leading to end of service:

Following Capcom's mighty 2026 releases, Resident Evil Requiem and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, I wanted to understand what went wrong for Exoprimal, so I hopped back on. Funnily enough, I was actually enjoying the game, despite it being a ghost town. Only nine players were active at the time, and it really felt like it. It's still a fun title though, which makes the end of service announcement quite sad, at least for me.

#4051. GTA 6 Won’t Let You Enter A Hostile Area The Same Way Twice

Ever since Grand Theft Auto 6 was released, countless players have been flooding social media with discoveries, comedic moments, and features that have managed to impress players who previously dismissed the series altogether. While most of these are entirely original to GTA 6 itself, some of the recently discovered mechanics are ones that seem more than a little familiar to stealth fans.

Although Rockstar has plenty of digs at other game studios and references to real-world franchises, one of the ways GTA 6 tackles repeat attempts at raiding a location bears a striking resemblance to those found in none other than Metal Gear Solid 5: The Phantom Pain of all places.

Added alongside the versatility of crime options scattered across Leonida comes in the form of criminal bases you can raid for goods like meth labs and other gang bases. While they seem straightforward at first, players like David Franklin on X were quick to discover that if you fail too many times going through a specific spot, the NPCs will react to it and prepare new defenses accordingly.

This isn't the only case either, as other players have reported similar instances like climbing over a spot of broken barbed wire and failing, only to come back and find a fresh piece tacked on, forcing them to find another way inside. It isn't just defenses either, as players have reported loot and enemy locations moving afterward too.

While you can find countless other examples of absurdly detailed mechanics and small features just by scrolling through the comments of posts like these, this specific mechanic is one that we've seen in more than a few games.

Most notably with Metal Gear Solid 5, which offered a similarly drastically expanded gameplay system compared to its predecessors, if you use a specific strategy like headshots or attacking at night too many times, enemies will actively react by starting to wear more helmets or equip additional night vision goggles.

People are spreading complete misinformation for a few likes when we should be celebrating how impressive the grand theft auto is in GTA 6.

Although far from the only game to have a similar system, with Hello Neighbor and Alien Isolation both having adaptive enemy AI reacting to your decisions, Metal Gear Solid definitely feels the most similar for the vibe of Grand Theft Auto, especially with plenty of comparisons to the classic franchise being made after GTA 6 significantly revamped its stealth mechanics.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4050. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4048. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#4047. Witchbrook Has Officially Gone Gold

The long-awaited cozy magical sim game Witchbrook has officially gone Gold, developer Chucklefish announced today. For those unfamiliar with the term “Gold," it generally means the game is complete and ready to be submitted to platforms for certification (and is less likely to be delayed).

Witchbrook is set to launch on January 28, ending a development cycle that stretches back nearly a decade. First teased in 2017, Witchbrook is a life-sim where players control a witch who begins life in the seaside town of Mossport. This includes making friends, finding love, and, most importantly, enrolling in Witchbrook College to master magic by taking classes and completing assignments.

We're delighted to announce that Witchbrook has GONE GOLD ALL PLATFORMS! 💛 We're can't for you all to join us on the journey on Jan 28th! ✨[image or embed]

Witchbrook is more or less Stardew Valley meets Hogwarts Legacy, as you can also start and run businesses, engage in seasonal events, and interact with fully fleshed-out citizens who have daily routines and schedules to consider. After a development cycle marked by long stretches of silence and several delays, those anticipating Witchbrook can breathe easier knowing the game will more than likely stick to its release date.

When Witchbrook launches on January 28, it will be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.

#4046. GTA 6's Physical Launch Has Been An Astronomical Success, Despite No Discs

All eyes have been on the launch of GTA 6 this month, with the game's so-called physical launch being a particularly interesting litmus test for the future of the industry.

It turns out that even without any discs, GTA 6 has proven to be a monumental success in terms of physical sales. This comes via Christopher Dring at The Game Business, who states that the game enjoyed the largest physical launch since 2019 in the UK, generating £32 million in revenue in just three days.

He goes on to state that GTA 6 is the "No.17 biggest physical game launch in the UK since records began in 1995".

In France, it's estimated that over 1 million physical copies were sold in the first three days, a figure that Dring states is comparable to GTA 5 back in 2013. In Spain, meanwhile, the game achieved the largest physical launch in the chart's history.

It's safe to say then that this has comfortably dwarfed pretty much anything that Nintendo has put out in recent years. Normally of course, we'd be celebrating such success – even if the game isn't actually available on Nintendo systems – but the fact that it's a code-in-a-box release raises a few eyebrows.

With GTA 6 being such a success, Sony will no doubt view this as validation that it made the right decision in ceasing the production of discs from 2028. Other large companies will also likely see it as proof that customers don't care about discs anymore, and will likely lean toward download codes much sooner than Sony's cut-off date.

Nintendo itself, meanwhile, probably won't do anything different – at least for the time being. Stats from recent financial reports indicate that Switch and Switch 2 players still value cartridges, with physical sales still making up close to half of the company's total first-party sales.

Still, it's a troubling result for folks who are still all-in on physical games. It certainly indicates that while there are plenty of folks who begrudge Sony's decision to stop the production of discs, there are many, many more people who just don't give a hoot.

GTA VI’s financial achievement is incredible, but comparing revenue without accounting for the price of admission isn’t exactly an apples-to-apples comparison.

Biggest launch by dollars doesn’t automatically mean biggest audience or biggest cultural event.

#4045. The Witcher 4 Dev Signs New 'Agreements' With Sony, But What Does It Mean For Xbox?

"This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook"

Michał Nowakowski has also now shared the following tweet about this:

Original Story: Last night, we saw some news starting to do the rounds about The Witcher 4 and its developer CD Projekt Red, with Chief Financial Officer Piotr Nielubowicz stating that the studio has entered into new "agreements" with Sony.

These agreements cover the presence of CDPR games on subscription services such as PlayStation Plus, but also "our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign" - which is the bit we're particularly interested in.

Here's a bit of the transcription via our friends at VGC:

"Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign."

"This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years."

A lot of people are now speculating that The Witcher 4's "collaboration" with Sony may be akin to what Take-Two has done with GTA 6, pushing the whole "plays best on PS5" campaign and restricting how Xbox is allowed to advertise the game. For example, GTA's launch trailer was solely focused around PS5 for an exclusive window.

It's important to highlight that this is just speculation though, and there may be aspects of these agreements that aren't exclusive at all. We've seen CDPR titles like Cyberpunk 2077 on Xbox Game Pass in the not too distant past, for example, so the PlayStation Plus agreement doesn't necessarily mean Game Pass is out the window.

Let's wait and see what happens with this, but just keep in mind that we could be looking at a situation where The Witcher 4 gets a bigger push on PlayStation than Xbox when it (hopefully) releases in 2028. We'll also leave you with a fun GTA comparison quote from joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski about the difference between Witcher 3 and 4!

"I’m not going to make a deep dive, full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6, but of course, we did look at the game, we did see the differences... we believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4. It’s been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better-looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game."

They'll be at Gamescom with Witcher 3's new DLC as well

News These Are The 70+ Most Important New Features In The Witcher 3 Remastered

What do you think these agreements mean? Let us know your thoughts in the comments section below.

[source videogameschronicle.com, via videogameschronicle.com]

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

It's the same thing with the "Play Best on PS5" campaign for GTA 6, which was completely dismantled by Digital Foundry's latest analysis. At this point, they're openly treating consumers like fools. Considering that the game is a multiplatform title, I find it pretty crazy that this kind of messaging is even allowed by competition authority and isn't considered false advertising.

The implication is clear: they're trying to make people believe the PS5 version offers the best experience, when the available evidence simply doesn't support that claim.

PlayStation has a habit of pushing the limits of what should be legally acceptable, and the company has been involved in numerous legal disputes over the years. I believe competition regulators should seriously examine this kind of marketing practice.

If a claim gives consumers a misleading impression about the quality or performance of a product compared to competing platforms, then it deserves scrutiny from the relevant authorities.

#4044. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

#4043. A Complete Guide To The Nauctis Commander Precons In MTG

The first set of 2027 brings with it four exciting new precons, and here's what we know about them so far.

We already know that 2027 will be the year of the Magic: The Gathering Commander precon, with at least 24 new decks arriving across six total sets. The first set of the year is Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, and we've already got a look at the four precons arriving with this underwater-themed set, and there's a lot to like.

We have a good idea of the theme for each deck, and another leak suggests a very powerful Commander ability is coming to an all-new Shark card.

The Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Commander precons are officially launching on Friday, February 5, 2027. If you are attending a prerelease event or have a good relationship with your local game store, you may be able to purchase your precons starting Friday, January 29, 2027.

The base editions of the Commander precons will cost $49.99, but no longer come with any foil borderless Commander cards. These have been moved to the premium editions of the decks, a new version exclusive to in-universe sets (Universes Beyond still has collector's editions). Premium edition decks not only include the foil borderless Commander cards, but are also printed entirely in traditional foil, and they cost $79.99 each.

We're at the end of 2026, and with all seven MTG sets now out, we're going to rank all the Commander precons we've seen so far.

Blood in the Water is the Shark deck that focuses on swinging wide with creatures and creating blood tokens, a returning mechanic that will play a big role for the creature in Nauctis.

A leak has suggested that the face Commander of this deck will have Eminence, a powerful ability that triggers both when your Commander is in play and in the Command Zone.

Based on what we've seen so far, this is the fastest, most aggressive deck of the bunch, and it looks like it will be a ton of fun to play, especially if that face Commander is packing such a powerful ability.

Group hug returns! Seal the Deal will have you offering your opponents something to stop them from attacking you. In this case, it appears to be treasure tokens, but not nearly enough has leaked about this deck for us to say anything for sure.

Seals will play a role for sure, but we also anticipate Octopuses and Otters could feature, too.

We haven't had a group hug precon since Ms. Bumbleflower in Bloomburrow, and that card went on to be quite the popular card in the format, so we're extremely excited to see what happens with the new Seal on the block.

We're expecting Terrors of the Abyss to be the huge, scary sea-creature deck, and this has been backed up by an early leak showcasing the face and backup Commander for the deck.

While far from official, the cards were revealed in Japanese marketing material that was quickly pulled, and it looks like Terrors of the Abyss will be led by a giant sea serpent called The Noble Serpent. It's a huge eight-mana card that has you mill four cards right at the beginning of the game while it is in your Command Zone. Then, whenever it is in play, at the end of your turn, it lets you bring a creature back from your graveyard to the battlefield for free (provided it's classed as a Sea Monster).

Much like with Seal the Deal, we don't know an awful lot about the Merfolk Regiment deck, other than what's printed on the box.

It appears to focus on going wide, meaning you'll swing with a lot of creatures to outnumber your opponent's defenders and get damage through.

Tap and convoke is also mentioned, meaning we may be able to tap creatures on the battlefield to cover part of the cost of casting additional, more powerful creatures, a mechanic that Merfolk are more than familiar with.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4042. I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

Generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games. I never find them convincing. Relationships build way too quickly, and usually all it takes to win someone over in an RPG or farming sim is a couple of conversations and a few gifts. In Grand Theft Auto VI, however, I'm extremely invested in the romance between Jason and Lucia, and it comes down to the game's quieter moments and slice-of-life mechanics.

If you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop. I ask an NPC about her hometown, sympathize with her tragic backstory, promise to be there for her, and then give her the book, cake, or mining resource she likes. Do it enough, and one day she'll approach me with the uncharacteristically heartfelt confession that she can't stop thinking about me. The process is too transparently mechanical: I can scan the dialogue options and instantly know which of the three sentences will boost my affinity rating the most. It feels less like an actual relationship and more like a long-term scheme to program someone into dating.

Many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be. The issue is scope and structure. Romantic relationships are nuanced and unique, but there often aren't enough resources during a game's development to represent more than the basic building blocks. Players are meant to suspend disbelief and fill in the gaps – even though you technically only spoke to that villager a few dozen times, you're married with a child, so you imagine it's actually been years.

Of course, this scope is the difference between Grand Theft Auto VI and these other games – Rockstar made time and space for everything in this world, and romance is no exception.

Since they're dating when the game begins, Jason and Lucia admittedly skip the courtship phase that many games focus on, but their relationship is still conditional and malleable – if you want them to like each other, you should be acting in their best interests. And while the mechanical aspect of their romance is still plenty visible, the actions to increase that meter are vastly expanded. There has been a lot of discussion about the early game, when you can prep for Lucia's release from prison by buying flowers or groceries, and while I like those gestures, they're not what sold me on the relationship. Say what you will about modern dating standards, but flowers and food are too easy – too obvious for me to feel connected to and invested in a couple.

When I played this section, I felt like Jason's hair looked a little unkempt, so I got a shave and a haircut. And, to my surprise, this improved his relationship with Lucia. She wasn't around and wouldn't see the results until later, but it still scored me partner points, as did repairing the roof, painting the bedroom walls, and even giving Jason's car a new paint job. These unexpected, specific tasks don't just fill up the relationship gauge – they communicate information about both characters. Lucia is really looking forward to getting out of prison, and having a finished house and a clean, put-together partner sets her in a better mood. Meanwhile, my actions establish that my version of Jason knows she likes these things and would do them without even asking.

Minor, specific tasks like these are romantic because they imply a degree of thoughtfulness that sidesteps the grand gestures expected of a long-awaited reunion. Yes, there should be apples in the fridge, but that's a basic need; knowing the exact conditions Lucia wants the house to be in makes me believe Jason actually knows her. It becomes even more effective – both in real relationships and in the credibility of the in-game partnership – when thoughtfulness is demonstrated on a day-to-day basis, in the quiet moments.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a long game with a slow, steady pace, leaving room for the intimate interactions other games wouldn't have time for. If you come home at the end of the day and see your partner watching TV, you can sit next to them and get a bonus. When they go to sleep, they'll call out to you and ask you to lie in bed and scroll on your phone with them. You can hold hands in public, buy each other clothes, and remember to text back promptly. There are large, dramatic moments and professions of love, yes, but players are likely to experience vastly more of these minor interactions than those scripted cutscenes.

Romance can be flashy, but it has to be more than that. It's nice to see the starring duo dance, drive, and shoot at foes during cutscenes. But it's the long car rides when Lucia reassures Jason that her mom likes him, or the evening on the couch when Jason talks about how he likes the way Lucia laughs, that make this relationship work narratively.

What are your favorite video game romances? Let us know in the comments!
