Sam Corcos is vibe-coding Legatum, a "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While DOGE itself is long dead, some of the officials appointed by the Elon Musk-backed organization remain part of the United States government. That includes Sam Corcos, who joined the Treasury Department as special advisor in 2025 and soon became chief information officer there. Corcos remains in that position amid a heavily scrutinized cybersecurity breach at the department, but that hasn't stopped him from finding the time to continue vibe-coding his Civilization clone.

Yes, Corcos is creating a game, in the loosest terms, called Legatum, which is a "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization." Taking specific inspiration from Civilization 6, it's "familiar on purpose," according to the GitHub readme, letting you choose a civilization and build alliances or make war on rivals as progress through nine eras and try to build the greatest empire of all.

"Legatum is built largely with AI coding agents, and all of its art is AI-generated," that readme explains. "Most of the art comes from OpenAI's image models through ChatGPT; the icons and heraldry are SVG drawn by scripts in this repository. The working files are public so that other people can learn from them."

Dozens upon dozens of updates have been made to Legatum in the past few days, a fact that has drawn some scrutiny given that the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, a bureau of the Treasury Department, is in the midst of dealing with a self-described "cybersecurity incident."

A notice on FinCEN's website notes that the breach has "resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline." While few details on this incident have been made public, a breach of a US bureau dedicated to fighting financial crime does seem like an 'all hands on deck' situation that would give the organization's CIO something more important to do.

For his part, Corcos tweets that "the computers are doing it on their own. Mostly Opus 5.5 orchestrating a bunch of iterative loops." But, as 404 Media notes, he's finding time to regularly give feedback to Claude on new features and tweaks that should be made for Legatum.

Using GitHub's issue tracker, users have noted a problem with the code: "Treasury CIO is too busy vibecoding instead of doing his job." Several comments seem to agree, but Corcos eventually closed the discussion as "off-topic," since the "tracker is for bugs and ideas about the Legatum game." This response was also generated by Claude.

#3942. Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang offers to return if that's best for the company and America, Nvidia board essentially say 'nah, we're all good'

New rulers impervious to highly persuasive message of 'come on, please give me my job back, go USA'

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

That last bit seems likely to have been said with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO."

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the company's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

#3941. Even the PS5 Pro is "not powerful enough" to run GTA 6 at 60FPS or 40FPS, Rockstar says

Don't expect GTA 6 to get an update supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's currently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other big productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.

"While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, said in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

Chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity."

The tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

The slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again."

If you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to New Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.

#3940. Final Fantasy Resonance Devs Surprised by How Many Fans Wanted a Traditional, Turn-Based RPG

Final Fantasy Resonance has been one of the most positively-received Square Enix games in ages — but its developers were never fully convinced that it would, er, resonate on the scale that it has.

Producer Keisuke Nakashima told Japanese outlet Game*Spark (as translated by Automaton): "I was surprised to see just how many people, not only in Japan but overseas as well, are eager for the kind of FF they remember from back in the day, with classic turn-based battles and pixel art."

Of course, this quote feeds into a debate that's been raging amongst fans of Final Fantasy for over a couple of decades at this point.

There are many who believe that the series has long since lost its way, pushing to innovate with more and more action-focused gameplay instead of drawing from the turn-based and command battle systems that helped establish the franchise as a world-beater in the first place.

Titles like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 are constantly brought up as living proof that turn-based RPGs can still be blockbusters — but Square Enix has only veered further and further away from Final Fantasy's traditional blueprint with each mainline instalment.

Resonance may be a lower-budget spin-off, but at least to some extent, it does go against the publisher's line of thinking that Final Fantasy must appeal to a "wider audience" if it's to maintain its flagship status.

"We figured [Resonance] was something we ourselves would enjoy, and that there would be players out there who’d feel the same way," says Nakashima.

Director Hiroto Furuya adds: "I thought this was a rather unconventional title, so I expected opinions on it might be divided."

He then references Resonance's foundations, having been built on the bones of now defunct mobile title Final Fantasy Brave Exvius: "I think the fact that a game with such an unusual background has been embraced by so many people is a positive for the industry as a whole, and I’m personally very happy to see it."

Without wanting to be overly critical of games I really enjoy, like Final Fantasy 16, I do think Square Enix has been guilty of chasing a goal that simply may not exist.

This mythical "wider audience" has been the downfall of many games over the years, and you can argue that Final Fantasy has chipped away at its own identity and strength of brand in the (pretty desperate) pursuit of new fans.

Resonance isn't going to sell millions upon millions of copies, but the way it's been embraced says a lot about the current state of Final Fantasy as a whole, I feel.

And remember, recent reports strongly suggested that the suits at Square Enix wanted Resonance to be a basic port of the aforementioned mobile title, presumably in a bid to keep costs down.

Are you glad Final Fantasy Resonance exists? Do you think Square Enix needs to learn from its success? Take a turn in the comments section below.

It's come to my attention that some of us aren't having a very fun time with the NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've seen videos and threads of players complaining about not being able to steal cars because of crack head drivers, getting hunted down by killer NPCs, and just generally having a harder time traversing Leonida because who knows what bloodthirsty beast hides behind each corner? And to this I say, your steak is too buttery? Your lobster too juicy?

My first interaction with one of the unfriendly residents of Leonida started when I accidentally bumped into their car. Because I am wholly unaware of my surroundings, I didn't even notice that anyone was mad at me as I listened to my pop songs and carried on driving towards my mission. Little did I know that right behind me was a four-wheeler with a driver who had steam coming out of her ears.

So I pull up to the side of the road, ready to head in and start my mission, when seemingly out of nowhere the four-wheeler comes barreling in, almost taking me out completely. The driver gets out and starts screaming about payback. I have no idea what I've done, but this is GTA 6, I'm not taking this slander. So I start swinging.

The fight ends with me knocking this lady out, but she doesn't go down without a fight. At one point, I actually thought that was it for me—taken out on the pavement by a soccer mum, what a way to go.

But even if I had taken a long sleep on the sidewalk, that would've been OK, because it's all part of the beautiful package that GTA 6 offers.

I don't want vapid NPCs that buckle at the first sight of a handgun, or have the object permanence of a goldfish. Filling Leonida with some actually competent, and dare I say dangerous NPCs makes this game infinitely more interesting. I like not knowing how one small action will ruin my whole day, or having to be a little wary of the people around me lest I want to incur a murderous chase across the city streets.

Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while.

I have a theory as to why players are pushing back against aggressive NPCs: they just don't like having to put in the effort after years of being able to do whatever they want in GTA Online. There's certainly some that will look back on the mostly timid NPCs of Los Santos and miss when all they had to do to steal a car was swing open its door and throw the limp driver out. Aside from shouting, there wasn't really anything a regular NPC could do to pose a threat to you back then.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Rockstar amped up the mayhem and carnage you could cause, turning it into a chaotic playground with few repercussions. GTA Online players have become accustomed to walking around like some vengeful god, wreaking havoc wherever or whenever they see fit, and only very occasionally dealing out mercy. Now these fickle deities have been forced to become human again.

A part of me understands the appeal. Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while. NPCs that actually have a backbone offer an experience that will keep me interested for far longer.

Plus, Leonida is based on Florida, do you honestly think you could terrorise the streets of Miami or Tampa Bay and walk out completely unscathed? Yeah, I thought as much.

#3938. Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

Administrators say "a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise"

Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Announced in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

The same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The company grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "currently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

#3937. GTA 6 won't let you use cheats until you complete the main story, and locks progression when you do

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

The way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

The true box office winner of Dunesday has been predicted by the Nielsen ratings, and it's none other than Avengers: Doomsday.

Per Deadline, NRG (National Research Group, owned by Nielsen) predicts that Doomsday will bring in $270 million at the global box office during its opening weekend. Dune 3 is predicted to bring in $75 million.

This is the highest projection NRG has ever recorded, with Spider-Man: Brand New Day being the second-highest. To date, Avengers: Endgame now holds the record second-highest opening weekend for any movie ever at $357.1M, having been beat out by Spider-Man: Brand New Day's $360 million.

Avengers: Doomsday tickets went on sale back in July for the special Infinity Vision screenings. It's worth noting that 60,000 more tickets were sold for the early Thursday screenings following the VisionQuest finale, which teases the return of Wanda Maximoff aka the Scarlet Witch. Wanda will indeed return in Doomsday, but she won't be, uh, herself... if you catch my drift.

Dune 3 tickets have been a bit of a nightmare for fans as they sold out almost immediately back in April, and then crashed several movie theater apps when more tickets were released back in August. Oh, and, when tickets did sell out in April... people started reselling them for up to $1000. The people yearn for sand.

Avengers: Doomsday and Dune 3 hit theaters on December 18. For more on the MCU, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#3935. Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

#3934. PC remains GTA 6's last hope for 60fps smoothness as Rockstar confirm such an option isn't coming to even the swankiest consoles

Poor little game boxes just can't handle it

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates."

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

#3933. PS Plus Essential Games for December 2026 Announced

These games will be available to claim until 4th January, 2027 after they’ve been added to the sub next week.

It’s the final update of 2026 and PS Plus Essential is going out with a bit of a bang in my opinion.

Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 + 4 is the most recent remake in Activision’s long-running skateboarding series, and a very good compilation at that.

We awarded it an 8/10 in our review, writing: “Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4 is another fantastic skateboarding title that revives some all-time classics, albeit with some caveats.”

Meanwhile, Dragon Ball XenoVerse 2 is arriving just ahead of its sequel next year. This game has received years of support, including a fairly recent PS5 port, included here as part of your subscription.

Of that PS5 version, we wrote in our 7/10 review: “The only problem with XenoVerse 2, here in 2024, is that its core gameplay has never truly evolved. Yes, more and more ways to upgrade and customise your character have been added over the years, but the actual combat feels basic and a touch too finicky by today's standards.”

Finally, Amnesia: The Bunker is an acclaimed horror game from specialists Frictional – and one we ultimately liked.

We said in our 7/10 review: “Amnesia: The Bunker sticks a little too close to what Frictional Games has been doing for over a decade now, but with a more free-form approach to gameplay, the team is back on the right track again.”

That rounds out the lineup for December, then – and 2026 as a whole? How are you feeling about PS Plus Essential this year? Let me know below.

Four years ago (oh my god) strategy RPG Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga rather impressed our reviewer Jon Bolding. He wrote that "novel tactical mechanics make this indie a contender for the best strategy RPG this year".

Well, buckle up, 2027, because Symphony of War 2 has broken cover with a promise to release next year, and it's coming courtesy of the strategy sommeliers at publisher Hooded Horse, which I take as a very good sign.

SOW2 looks set to continue the Fire-Emblem-ish framework of its predecessor, tasking you with recruiting a gaggle of heroes to wage war with (and possibly compose symphonies, who's to say?) in "a world filled with political intrigue, betrayal, and tense, large-scale tactical battles". Which is a lot like our world, really.

It all looks very nice indeed. In the announcement trailer, we get glimpses of its squad-based combat and anime cutscenes, and I am officially into both. The art is poppy and distinctive, at some point an age-of-sail warship transforms into some kind of German WW1 destroyer, and the overworld triggers the regions in my brain devoted to thinking about Heroes of Might and Magic. Check, check, and check.

"Anime cutscenes!?" I hear you cry. "That sounds like the kind of thing that bespeaks a dense tapestry of lore I'll need to get to grips with first!" Well, apparently not. I am informed by Symphony of War 2's Steam page that the devs have no expectation you know what a "Nephilim Saga" even is before you pick this game up. "Symphony of War 2 is a standalone experience set several generations after the events of the first game—it can be enjoyed without having played Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga". The game's tale of a fallen empire trying to un-fall can be enjoyed single-serve.

#3931. GTA 6's Japanese version only partially obscures male nudity by putting Jason in a thong, seemingly due to regional censorship

GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and New Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ

Another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," he wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

#3930. Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

It "ticks many of the boxes", despite the funding problems

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the new team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.
